c: Stride Athletics, a running and fitness store with six locations
s: Stride Athletics' sales are flat even though foot traffic is up. The store manager says too many associates simply point customers to the wall of shoes and then ring up the sale without learning what the customer needs.
The store manager (judge) wants you to explain the nature of selling, how an associate can build a loyal clientele, and why customer service is part of the selling relationship.
p: Explain the nature and scope of the selling function
Explain the selling process
Explain key factors in building a clientele
Explain the role of customer service as a component of selling relationships
n: Selling is helping customers solve a need with a product, not pushing one
Describes steps: greet, determine needs, present features and benefits, handle concerns, close, follow up
Names trust, repeat contact, product knowledge and fair treatment as building a clientele
Service after the sale (fit checks, returns, follow-up) brings customers back
q: A customer says the shoe they like is too expensive. What do you say?
How do you decide when to stop selling and let a customer think?

c: Sunrise Bakery, a family bakery with two locations
s: Sunrise Bakery is launching a seasonal pumpkin pastry line next month. The owner has only a small budget and wants the new line to be the talk of town by the first weekend.

The owner (judge) wants you to explain the elements of the promotional mix, which promotional activities would work best for a local bakery, and how to make sure the message is consistent wherever customers see it.
m: the owner's office above the bakery
p: Identify the elements of the promotional mix
Explain types of advertising media
Describe word-of-mouth channels used to communicate with targeted audiences
Explain the importance of coordinating elements in advertisements
n: Advertising, sales promotion, public relations, personal selling and digital
Suggests local social media, window displays, sample tastings, flyers
Encourages reviews, referral perks and shareable photos
Uses the same look, offer and message across signage, social and in-store
q: How will you know if the promotion worked?
What is the risk of promoting a product that sells out quickly?

c: Urban Loft, a home décor retailer
s: Urban Loft's new line of ceramic lamps has been on shelves for six weeks and sales are slow. A competitor sells a similar lamp for $15 less online, but Urban Loft's cost is high and margins are already tight.
The merchandising director (judge) wants you to explain what affects a business's pricing decisions, why pricing must follow legal and ethical rules, and what you would recommend for the lamps.
p: Explain the nature and scope of the pricing function
Explain factors affecting pricing decisions
Describe the role of business ethics in pricing
Explain legal considerations for pricing
n: Pricing sets the value customers pay and affects profit and image
Factors: costs, competition, demand, brand, perceived value, promotions
Honest pricing: no deceptive 'was' prices or hidden fees
Mentions laws against price fixing and false advertising
q: Would you lower the price, add a bundle, or do something else? Why?
What could happen if the lamp's price is too low?

c: Greenlane Outdoors, a start-up making reusable travel containers
s: Greenlane Outdoors sells to hikers online but wants to reach new customers, including commuters and students. The company has a small team and a modest budget.
The marketing manager (judge) wants you to explain how a company identifies its market, what a marketing plan includes, and how a situation analysis helps the company decide where to focus.
p: Explain the concept of market and market identification
Explain the nature of marketing plans
Explain the role of situation analysis in the marketing planning process
Explain the nature of sales forecasts
n: Defines a target market by who needs the product, where they are and what they value
Plan includes goals, target market, strategies, budget and measures
Situation analysis looks at strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, threats and competitors
Forecast sales from past data, trends and planned promotions
q: Which new group would you target first, commuters or students? Why?
What would you do if actual sales came in far below the forecast?

c: Nimbus Tech Accessories, a maker of phone cases and chargers
s: Nimbus Tech Accessories' best-selling phone case is getting older and sales are falling. The company can redesign it, bundle it with a charger, or develop a new line.

The product manager (judge) wants you to explain the nature of product management, what product life cycles mean for marketing decisions, and how Nimbus can use branding and customer feedback to decide what to do.
p: Explain the nature and scope of the product/service management function
Identify the impact of product life cycles on marketing decisions
Describe the nature of product bundling
Describe the role of customer voice in branding
n: Product management plans, develops, improves and retires products to meet customer needs
Introduction, growth, maturity and decline each call for different promotion and pricing
Bundling raises perceived value and average sale
Reviews, surveys and returns show what customers want and strengthen the brand
q: How would you decide between redesigning the case and launching a new product?
What would you do with the old case when a new one comes out?
